summary.text: Kent Udell, a Democratic retired professor of mechanical engineering who taught at the University of Utah and UC Berkeley, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Utah's 3rd Congressional District to Republican Rep. Celeste Maloy.
He has also served on federal advisory boards and said corruption in federal politics prompted his run.

paragraphs.text: Udell was born in Lehi, Utah, and now lives in Moab.

He earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Utah State University in 1974, then a master's degree in 1978 and a doctorate in 1980 from the University of Utah, according to the University of Utah mechanical engineering department.
Udell built his career as a professor of engineering, teaching at the University of California, Berkeley and the University of Utah, and he has served on federal advisory boards.

He also worked in the petroleum industry, which he told the Deseret News would help him act as a bridge between the federal government and the district's communities, including Uintah County, coal country and the tourism industry.
Udell entered the race after retiring, saying he was prompted by what he described as corruption of big money in politics and of the political system itself.
He advanced to the general election without appearing on a primary ballot after the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary was canceled.
He received 35.3% of the vote to Celeste Maloy's 57.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
